BiblicalUsage: The plain sense of héx is six. It comes up 13 times, and the passages from Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John show how steadily Scripture uses it. I do not find a second, secret meaning hiding behind it.
TheologicalSignificance: héx matters to me because six is the number of man — always one short of seven. I read this as a reminder that God’s words mean what they say, and I can trust them.
RelatedEvents: Transfiguration; Jesus Rejected at Nazareth; Jesus Turns Water into Wine at Cana
